title.rendered: I Will Pour Out My Spirit: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: I will pour out my Spirit on all people. The prophecy is older than the church. Joel saw it eight hundred years before Pentecost. The promise stood.

content.rendered:
I will pour out my Spirit on all people. The prophecy is older than the church. Joel saw it eight hundred years before Peter quoted it on the day of Pentecost. The promise was always going to be kept.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, May 17, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And afterward, I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.”
Joel 2:28 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Eight hundred years. That is roughly how long the gap was between the prophecy of Joel and the morning the prophecy was fulfilled. Eight hundred years of waiting between the promise and Pentecost. Eight hundred years in which the Spirit of God moved on chosen prophets, kings, and judges but had never been poured out on all flesh. And then, one ordinary morning in Jerusalem, the wait ended.

Joel saw it first. In the middle of a book about devastation and locust plagues, the prophet stops and looks down the corridor of time. He sees a day coming when God will not give His Spirit by careful measure to a few. He will pour Him out. Not drip. Not sprinkle. Pour. On sons and daughters. On the old and the young. On servants. On all flesh.

When Peter stood up on Pentecost morning with the sound of rushing wind still ringing in his ears, he did not invent something new. He pointed to something old. “This,” he said, “is what was spoken by the prophet Joel.” Eight centuries of waiting, and Peter could finally say: this is what He promised. This is the day.

We are one week away from Pentecost Sunday, and this week we will walk slowly toward that morning. We will look at the promises Jesus made about the Spirit before He left. We will look at the upper room where the disciples waited. We will look at the fire that fell on the day of Pentecost itself. And we will look at the church the Spirit birthed and what it means for us today.

But begin here. Begin with Joel. Begin with the long view. The Spirit of God who lives in every believer in Christ today is not a new arrangement God thought up in the first century. He is the fulfillment of a promise that was already old when Joel spoke it. The Father had always intended to dwell with His people. The cross opened the way. Pentecost was the day He arrived. And He has not left.

If you belong to Christ today, the Spirit poured out at Pentecost is the same Spirit who lives in you. Not a smaller version. Not a leftover from the original outpouring. The same Spirit, the same fullness, the same promise. Walk this week with that truth anchored in your heart.

Prayer

Father, thank You that the promise You spoke through Joel was not forgotten. You poured out Your Spirit on the day of Pentecost just as You said You would, and the same Spirit lives in me today because of what Jesus has done. Open my heart this week to walk slowly toward Pentecost and remember the wonder of what You have given me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The Spirit poured out at Pentecost is the Spirit who lives in me. He was promised through Joel, fulfilled at Pentecost, and given to me through Jesus. I do not have a smaller version. I have the same Spirit, the same fullness, the same promise. I walk into this week anchored to that truth.
